intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience includes a scenic gondola ride to the pod suspended above the canyon and is a must-do for adrenaline seekers visiting Queenstown.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most spectacular and famous one-day walks, crossing volcanic terrain with emerald crater lakes, steaming vents, and panoramic views of the Central Plateau. The 19.4 km trail passes the active Mount Ngauruhoe and offers otherworldly landscapes that inspired the Lord of the Rings films.

experiences.name: Milford Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Embark on a multi-day guided or independent hike along the world-famous Milford Track, a 53.5 km trail through Fiordland National Park. Trek through ancient rainforests, past cascading waterfalls including the stunning Sutherland Falls, and over the dramatic MacKinnon Pass with breathtaking alpine views.

experiences.name: Roys Peak Track Hike
experiences.description: Conquer the iconic Roys Peak trail above Lake Wānaka for one of the most photographed panoramic views in New Zealand. The 16 km round-trip hike rewards trekkers with sweeping vistas of Lake Wānaka, Mount Aspiring National Park, and the surrounding Southern Alps, especially magical at sunrise.

experiences.name: Shotover Canyon Swing
experiences.description: Experience the world's highest cliff jump and canyon swing, launching 109 meters above the wild Shotover River in Queenstown. With over 70 jump styles to choose from, this thrilling activity combines freefall with a massive pendulum swing through a dramatic schist rock canyon, offering an unforgettable adrenaline rush.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch or Queenstown airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange budget shuttle or public bus transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into your beachfront accommodation, and get a good night's rest after the flight.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport — look for a food court option or a pre-packed sandwich under NZD $15 before heading to the resort

day_by_day.notes: Late arrival — keep Day 1 completely free of scheduled activities. Confirm shuttle or bus transfer in advance to save money vs. taxis. Pack a snack in your carry-on to avoid expensive airport food.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a slow start, take a free self-guided walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Breathe in the fresh South Island air, explore the shoreline, and get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest town centre on foot or by local bus. Visit the local i-SITE visitor centre (free) to pick up maps, trail guides, and budget tips. Browse local supermarkets (Pak'nSave or Countdown) to stock up on groceries and snacks for the week — a key budget strategy.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal back at the resort using groceries. Spend the evening planning your hiking days ahead, download offline maps (Maps.me or AllTrails), and charge all devices. Early bedtime to reset your body clock.

meals.breakfast: Free or included breakfast at resort if available, or instant oats and fruit from the supermarket (under NZD $5)
meals.lunch: Supermarket deli — grab a fresh roll or sushi pack for around NZD $5–8
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or rice dish cooked at the resort kitchen — budget NZD $8–10 total

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is a gentle recovery and prep day. Stocking up at a supermarket early in the trip will save significant money on food throughout the 13 days. Ask the resort about free or low-cost local walks nearby.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the Roys Peak Track Hike above Lake Wānaka — one of New Zealand's most iconic and photographed viewpoints. Start early (6:00–7:00 AM) to beat the crowds and the midday heat. The trail is 16 km return with 1,279 m elevation gain. Bring at least 2 litres of water, packed snacks, and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue ascending to the summit (approximately 1,578 m) for breathtaking 360-degree panoramic views over Lake Wānaka and the surrounding mountain ranges. Take your time at the top — this is the iconic Instagram viewpoint. Begin the descent back down in the early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the trailhead by late afternoon. Drive or bus back toward the resort area. Soak tired legs in the ocean or a warm shower. Enjoy a well-earned relaxing evening at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-hike breakfast at the resort — porridge, banana, and peanut butter toast (self-catered, NZD $4–6)
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — sandwiches, trail mix, energy bars, and fruit prepared the night before (NZD $6–8)
meals.dinner: Wānaka town has great budget options — try Kai Whaka Pai food truck or grab fish and chips from a local takeaway for NZD $12–18

day_by_day.notes: Roys Peak Track is seasonal — it is closed during lambing season (October to mid-November in some years), so confirm the track is open before going. Wear sturdy hiking boots. The hike takes 5–6 hours return. Start as early as possible. No public toilets on the track — use facilities at the carpark beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery morning — take a flat, easy walk along the Lake Wānaka waterfront (free). The lakeside path is scenic and gentle on tired muscles from Roys Peak. Visit the free Wānaka Tree (the famous lone willow tree in the lake) for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Puzzling World attraction in Wānaka (entry around NZD $16–20 — one of the more affordable paid attractions in the area). Alternatively, keep it free by visiting the Wānaka Outlet and browsing the lakefront park. Consider renting a kayak or paddleboard on the lake for NZD $20–30/hour for a fun afternoon activity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Self-cater dinner using groceries. Spend the evening researching and preparing for the Tongariro Alpine Crossing coming up later in the trip.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — eggs on toast or cereal at the resort (NZD $4–5)
meals.lunch: Supermarket lunch — wrap, fruit, and a drink (NZD $8–10)
meals.dinner: Self-catered stir-fry or noodle dish at resort (NZD $8–10)

day_by_day.notes: Day 4 is a lighter activity day to allow leg muscles to recover from Roys Peak. Stay hydrated and consider stretching or a gentle yoga session in the morning. Confirm transport logistics for upcoming days.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — depart early toward Queenstown (approximately 1 hour from Wānaka area). Queenstown is the adventure capital of the world and home to some of the best budget bungee jumping experiences. Check into budget accommodation or return to resort if within range. Walk the Queenstown lakefront promenade (free) and soak in views of The Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Queenstown Gardens (free entry) — a beautiful peninsula park with walking paths, rose gardens, and lake views. Browse the central Queenstown mall and visitor centre. Research and book your bungee jump for the following day to lock in the best price (AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy is the world's first commercial bungee site — prices from NZD $135–165).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant but budget-friendly food scene. The Gorge Road area and Remarkables Market (if running on weekends) offer great value options.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before travel (NZD $4–5)
meals.lunch: Fergburger is iconic but pricey — opt for the Queenstown Night Market or a supermarket wrap (NZD $8–12)
meals.dinner: Vudu Larder and Bakery or The Cow restaurant for budget pasta dishes (NZD $18–25) — a treat night in Queenstown

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown is the most expensive town in New Zealand — be mindful of spending. Book bungee in advance online for potential discounts. Many Queenstown viewpoints and walks are completely free and spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: BUNGEE JUMPING DAY — Head to the world-famous Kawarau Bridge Bungy (43 m drop over the Kawarau River) operated by AJ Hackett. This is the world's first commercial bungee jumping site and an absolute bucket-list experience. Arrive early for your pre-booked slot. The jump itself takes seconds but the adrenaline lasts all day. Spectating is free if friends want to watch.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, take the free Skyline Gondola walk (hike up Bob's Peak instead of paying NZD $40 for the gondola — the walk takes about 45 minutes and the views are identical and free). Enjoy panoramic views over Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu from the top.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungee jump with a budget dinner in Queenstown. Explore the lively waterfront area. Consider a free evening walk along the lake under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-jump breakfast — banana, toast, and water (no heavy meals before bungee). Self-catered NZD $3–5
meals.lunch: Post-jump treat — grab a burger or fish and chips on the waterfront (NZD $12–18)
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market (Thursday–Sunday) for affordable diverse street food options (NZD $10–15) or supermarket self-cater

day_by_day.notes: Do NOT eat a heavy meal before bungee jumping. Wear comfortable, secure clothing and closed-toe shoes. Your jump video and photos cost extra (NZD $50–80) — decide in advance if it fits your budget. The Kawarau Bridge site also has a free viewing platform for non-jumpers.

day_by_day.morning: Take the free Queenstown Hill Time Walk (3.5 hours return, 500 m elevation gain) for sweeping views over the entire Queenstown Basin. A fantastic free alternative to paid viewpoints. Start early to avoid the heat. The trail begins near the town centre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Queenstown waterfront and Steamer Wharf area. Visit the free Kiwi Birdlife Park viewing areas (full entry NZD $49 — skip if on tight budget) or enjoy the free lakeside areas. Consider a short scenic drive to Arrowtown (20 minutes from Queenstown) — a charming historic gold-mining village with free walking trails and the free Lakes District Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Return to base. Self-cater dinner. Rest and prepare for the big travel day to the Tongariro region coming up.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats and fruit (NZD $4–5)
meals.lunch: Arrowtown has a great bakery — grab a meat pie and drink for NZD $8–12
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty pasta with vegetables (NZD $8–10) — fuel up for upcoming hikes

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown in November is beautiful — the autumn colours may still be lingering on the trees. The free Arrow River Bridges Track in Arrowtown is a lovely 2-hour easy walk if you have energy. Start planning logistics for the Tongariro Alpine Crossing transport.

day_by_day.morning: Major travel day — depart South Island accommodation early and travel north. The Tongariro Alpine Crossing is located in the North Island (Tongariro National Park), so this requires either a flight from Queenstown to Auckland/Wellington then onward, or a ferry crossing and drive. Book the cheapest option in advance — budget airlines like Air New Zealand or Jetstar often have deals under NZD $80–120 one way. Aim to arrive in the Tongariro/Taupo region by evening.
day_by_day.afternoon: In-transit. If flying, arrive at the airport with time to spare. Browse airport for budget food options. If driving/bussing via ferry, enjoy the scenic Interislander or Bluebridge ferry crossing through the Marlborough Sounds (approximately 3.5 hours, budget NZD $50–80 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at budget accommodation near Tongariro National Park (Whakapapa Village, National Park township, or Turangi). Check in and prepare all gear for the Tongariro Alpine Crossing the following morning. Lay out hiking clothes, fill water bottles, and pack a full trail lunch the night before.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure (NZD $4–5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or airport/ferry food court — budget NZD $10–15
meals.dinner: National Park township has a small selection of cafes and a Four Square supermarket — grab supplies and self-cater or try the Schnapps Bar for a budget meal (NZD $15–22)

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest travel day of the trip. Book all transport well in advance for the best budget prices. The National Park township near Tongariro has very limited dining options — stocking up at a supermarket in Taupo or Turangi if passing through is strongly recommended. Confirm shuttle booking for Tongariro Alpine Crossing (mandatory — no private vehicle parking at trailhead). Shuttle costs NZD $35–45 return.

day_by_day.morning: TONGARIRO ALPINE CROSSING DAY — One of New Zealand's Great Walks and most spectacular one-day hikes. Catch the early shuttle from National Park or Whakapapa Village (depart 6:00–7:00 AM). The crossing is 19.4 km one-way through dramatic volcanic terrain including the active Mt Ngauruhoe (Mt Doom from Lord of the Rings), the Red Crater, Emerald Lakes, and Blue Lake. Begin the ascent through the South Crater in the morning — the most challenging section.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the highlight of the crossing — the stunning Red Crater summit (1,868 m) and the iconic vivid Emerald Lakes below. Descend through the Blue Lake area and the long but rewarding trail down through forest to the Ketetahi car park. The full crossing takes 6–8 hours depending on fitness and photo stops.
day_by_day.evening: Shuttle back to accommodation. Shower, rest, and elevate tired legs. A well-earned early dinner and early bedtime — this will be one of the most physically demanding days of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Very early light breakfast before shuttle — banana, energy bar, toast (NZD $4–5). No time for a big meal.
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch is essential — there are NO food services on the track. Prepare the night before: sandwiches, nuts, chocolate, dried fruit, energy gels (NZD $8–10)
meals.dinner: Return to National Park township — Schnapps Bar or self-cater a hearty recovery meal (NZD $15–20)

day_by_day.notes: CRITICAL: The Tongariro Alpine Crossing is a ONE-WAY track — you MUST pre-book shuttle transport for both ends. Carry at least 2–3 litres of water (no reliable water sources on the track). Weather on the crossing can change rapidly — check the MetService forecast the night before and morning of. If weather is rated 'poor' or 'severe', consider postponing by one day as the crossing can be dangerous in bad conditions. Wear proper hiking boots — not sneakers. Sunscreen and a warm layer are essential even in November.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the Tongariro Alpine Crossing. Sleep in and have a relaxed breakfast. Take a short, easy walk around Whakapapa Village or the lower Tongariro National Park tracks — the Silica Rapids Track (2.5 hours return, flat and easy) is a beautiful free option through native beech forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or bus to Taupo (approximately 1 hour from National Park). Taupo sits on the shores of Lake Taupo — New Zealand's largest lake. Visit the free Huka Falls — one of New Zealand's most visited natural attractions. The thundering falls on the Waikato River are stunning and completely free to visit. Walk the short 10-minute path from the car park.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Taupo town centre. Browse the lakefront and enjoy sunset views over Lake Taupo toward the Tongariro volcanic peaks. Self-cater dinner or find a budget eatery in Taupo.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered recovery breakfast — eggs, toast, and coffee at accommodation (NZD $5–7)
meals.lunch: Taupo has great budget options — try the Taupo Supermarket or a local bakery for a pie and drink (NZD $8–12)
meals.dinner: Replete Eatery in Taupo for affordable healthy meals, or self-cater at accommodation (NZD $12–18)

day_by_day.notes: Day 10 is intentionally lighter to allow full recovery from the Tongariro crossing. Huka Falls is genuinely spectacular and completely free — don't miss it. If feeling energetic, the Spa Thermal Park in Taupo offers a FREE natural hot river pool (the Otumuheke Stream meets the Waikato River) — perfect for soothing sore hiking muscles.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Taupo and begin the journey back south toward the South Island or explore more of the central/southern North Island. If heading back to the South Island, aim to catch a morning ferry or flight. Alternatively, stop at Rotorua (1 hour north of Taupo) for a brief visit to the free Kuirau Park — a public geothermal park with boiling mud pools and steam vents, completely free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue travel south. If back on the South Island, travel toward Christchurch or the Marlborough Sounds region. The Marlborough region offers free scenic drives through wine country (Marlborough is famous for Sauvignon Blanc). Stop at free lookout points along Queen Charlotte Drive for stunning Sounds views.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at or near Aegean Bliss Resort or budget accommodation in the Marlborough/Nelson area. Rest and plan the final two days of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before travel (NZD $4–5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop — Marlborough has excellent roadside stalls selling fresh produce cheaply (NZD $8–12)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at accommodation using supermarket groceries (NZD $8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Day 11 is primarily a travel and transition day. Keep costs low by packing food for the journey. If passing through Marlborough wine country, many wineries offer free cellar door tastings — a fun free activity even if you only try a small amount.

day_by_day.morning: Final full hiking day — explore the Abel Tasman National Park coastal track if in the Nelson/Marlborough area, or the Banks Peninsula Track near Christchurch. The Abel Tasman Coast Track is one of New Zealand's Great Walks — day sections are free to walk without hut bookings. The Marahau to Anchorage section (approximately 3–4 hours one way) offers stunning golden beaches and coastal forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Abel Tasman coastal track or return via water taxi (NZD $35–45) for a scenic ocean journey back to Marahau. Alternatively, explore the free Christchurch Botanic Gardens (one of the best free attractions in New Zealand) if based in Christchurch — 30 hectares of stunning gardens along the Avon River.
day_by_day.evening: Final splurge dinner — treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal to celebrate completing the trip. Christchurch has excellent mid-range dining options. The Riverside Market in Christchurch has diverse food stalls at reasonable prices (NZD $15–25).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hearty breakfast before hiking (NZD $5–7)
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch for the Abel Tasman or a cafe near the Botanic Gardens (NZD $10–15)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner — Riverside Market Christchurch or a local favourite restaurant (NZD $20–30 as a final treat)

day_by_day.notes: Abel Tasman National Park requires a water taxi booking in advance during peak season (November is peak season). Book early. The park has no roads — access is by foot or boat only. If the weather is poor, the Christchurch Botanic Gardens and free Canterbury Museum are excellent full-day indoor/sheltered alternatives.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in New Zealand — pack bags and check out of accommodation. Take one last free walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort or explore a final free local attraction. If in Christchurch, visit the free Cardboard Cathedral (Re:START Container Mall area) — a symbol of Christchurch's rebuild after the 2011 earthquake and a genuinely moving free attraction.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport for departure. Allow extra time for check-in and baggage. Browse duty-free for any last-minute New Zealand souvenirs (Whittaker's chocolate is an affordable and iconic NZ gift). Reflect on an incredible 13 days of hiking, bungee jumping, and South Island adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart New Zealand. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast using remaining groceries — clear out the fridge! (NZD $4–5)
meals.lunch: Airport food court or use remaining cash/groceries for a packed airport lunch (NZD $10–15)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check out times are typically 10:00–11:00 AM — confirm with Aegean Bliss Resort. Use up any remaining New Zealand dollars on groceries, snacks, or small souvenirs before departure as NZD is difficult to exchange at good rates overseas. Leave a review for any budget accommodation or experiences that helped fellow budget travellers.

day_by_day.morning: No activities - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch or Queenstown Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange pre-booked transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack from the airport or a 24-hour convenience store near the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange an airport transfer or rental car pickup before arrival. Keep Day 1 light — rest is essential after a long-haul flight. Confirm resort check-in details in advance as arrival is after 10 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront to orient yourself and breathe in the fresh South Island air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area around the resort. Visit a nearby scenic lookout or coastal walking track for a gentle 1–2 hour introductory hike to stretch your legs and adjust to the time zone.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest town center for dinner. Browse the local shops and waterfront area to get a feel for the region.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or mid-range priced (~NZD $20–$30)
meals.lunch: Casual café near the beachfront — try a classic Kiwi meat pie or fish and chips (~NZD $15–$20)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in town — try New Zealand lamb or fresh local seafood (~NZD $35–$55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Do not over-schedule. Drink plenty of water and get to bed early to beat jet lag before the adventure begins.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a scenic bus transfer toward Queenstown (if not already based there). Stop at any scenic viewpoints along the way such as Lake Dunstan or the Kawarau Gorge. Arrive in Queenstown and check out the lakefront Queenstown Gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Shotover Canyon Swing — experience the world's highest cliff jump and canyon swing, launching 109 meters above the wild Shotover River. This adrenaline-pumping activity takes approximately 2–3 hours including briefing and multiple swing options.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your first big thrill in Queenstown's vibrant town center. Walk along the lakefront promenade and enjoy the stunning views of the Remarkables mountain range at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a grab-and-go from a local bakery for an early start (~NZD $10–$15)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or café stop en route to Queenstown (~NZD $15–$20)
meals.dinner: Fergburger — Queenstown's legendary burger institution, a must-visit (~NZD $15–$20)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Shotover Canyon Swing well in advance as it sells out quickly in summer (November). Wear comfortable, secure clothing. Weight and health restrictions apply — check the operator's website before booking.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and prepare for the ultimate adrenaline experience — the Nevis Bungy Jump. Transfer via the dedicated Nevis bus from central Queenstown (~45 minutes). At 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge, this is New Zealand's highest bungy jump. Briefing and jump take approximately 3 hours total.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown. Decompress and celebrate with a gondola ride up Bob's Peak on the Skyline Gondola for panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. Optionally try the luge tracks at the top.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a well-earned sit-down dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Queenstown. Reflect on two days of incredible thrills.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at a Queenstown café before the Nevis transfer — try avocado toast or a full Kiwi breakfast (~NZD $18–$25)
meals.lunch: Restaurant at the top of the Skyline Gondola — buffet with panoramic lake views (~NZD $35–$45)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant or The Bunker — upscale mid-range dining with New Zealand produce (~NZD $45–$65 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires advance booking and a minimum weight of 45kg, maximum 127kg. Wear warm layers as the gorge can be cool. Photography and video packages are available to purchase on the day.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Wānaka (approximately 1 hour via the Crown Range — the highest sealed road in New Zealand with spectacular views). Stop at the Crown Range Summit Lookout for photos. Arrive in Wānaka and check in to mid-range accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Roys Peak Track Hike — an iconic 16 km return trail with 1,279 meters of elevation gain above Lake Wānaka. Start in the early afternoon (aim to begin by 1–2 PM at the latest) to reach the summit and return before dark. The hike takes approximately 5–6 hours return.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the trailhead as the golden hour light bathes Lake Wānaka. Drive back into town, shower and rest tired legs. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in Wānaka.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Queenstown before departure (~NZD $18–$25)
meals.lunch: Pack your own trail lunch — sandwiches, energy bars, fruit from a local supermarket (~NZD $10–$15)
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen or Kika in Wānaka — casual, quality mid-range dining (~NZD $35–$50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Roys Peak is open from October to April (closed during lambing season May–October). Carry at least 2 liters of water per person, sunscreen, and layers. The track is well-marked but steep. Start early enough to complete before dark — November has long daylight hours (sunset ~9 PM).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover in Wānaka. Take a gentle flat walk around the shores of Lake Wānaka — the 7 km loop around the lake is perfect for tired legs. Visit the famous 'That Wānaka Tree' (the lone willow tree in the lake) for iconic photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Wānaka town. Visit Puzzling World — a quirky local attraction with optical illusions and a giant maze. Browse local galleries and boutique shops along the lakefront.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a lakeside bar in Wānaka — the lake views at golden hour are extraordinary. Enjoy a relaxed dinner before preparing for the big multi-day hike ahead.

meals.breakfast: Wānaka's Beechwood Café or Federal Diner — known for excellent brunch (~NZD $20–$30)
meals.lunch: Grab a burger or wrap from a local café or food truck by the lake (~NZD $15–$20)
meals.dinner: Ritual Café or Bistro Gentil — good mid-range options with local wine (~NZD $35–$55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use today to do laundry, repack your bag for the Milford Track, and purchase any last-minute supplies. You'll need to carry everything on the track so pack light but smart. Confirm your Milford Track booking and transport arrangements.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Wānaka to Te Anau (approximately 2.5 hours via Queenstown). Te Anau is the gateway town to Fiordland and the starting point for the Milford Track. Check in to a Te Anau lodge or hostel. Visit the DOC Visitor Centre to collect your hut passes and receive a track briefing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau town. Take a short walk along the lakefront of Lake Te Anau — the largest lake on the South Island. Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves by boat for a magical underground experience (book in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Prepare your pack for the Milford Track. Lay out all gear, food supplies, and confirm your hut bookings. Get an early night — the track starts tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Wānaka before the drive (~NZD $18–$25)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or café stop in Queenstown en route (~NZD $15–$20)
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau — excellent local game and seafood in a cozy setting (~NZD $40–$60 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Track is a Great Walk requiring advance DOC bookings (huts sell out months ahead — confirm your booking before the trip). The track runs 53.5 km over 4 days. Independent walkers must carry all food. The track is walked south to north: Glade Wharf to Sandfly Point.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Te Anau Downs boat ramp across Lake Te Anau to Glade Wharf (the track start). The ferry departs around 2 PM so spend the morning doing final pack checks and a hearty breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ferry to Glade Wharf and begin the Milford Track. Day 1 is a gentle 5 km walk through beech forest along the Clinton River to Clinton Hut. Arrive at the hut, settle in, and meet fellow trampers.
day_by_day.evening: Cook dinner in the hut kitchen, share stories with other hikers, and enjoy the pristine wilderness atmosphere. Rangers may give an evening talk about the track and local ecology.

meals.breakfast: Big cooked breakfast at your Te Anau accommodation to fuel up (~NZD $20–$30)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on the ferry or at Glade Wharf (~NZD $10 — self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hut dinner — dehydrated meals or pre-packed food carried in (~NZD $10–$15 per meal)

day_by_day.notes: DOC huts have gas cookers, running water, and flush toilets but no electricity. Bring a headlamp, warm layers, and rain gear — Fiordland receives some of the highest rainfall in the world. Sandflies are notorious; bring strong insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: The longest day on the track: 16.5 km from Clinton Hut to Mintaro Hut. Walk up the Clinton Valley through stunning beech forest with views of towering mountains and waterfalls. Pass the famous Bus Stop shelter and the junction to Hidden Lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up toward Mintaro Hut at the foot of Mackinnon Pass. The scenery becomes increasingly dramatic with alpine meadows and glacial valleys. Arrive at Mintaro Hut (elevation 950m) in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rest tired muscles, cook dinner, and admire the mountain views from the hut. Weather permitting, take a short stroll around the hut area at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked hut breakfast — oats, muesli, or instant porridge (~self-catered)
meals.lunch: Trail snacks and packed lunch eaten on the track — energy bars, crackers, cheese, dried fruit
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hut dinner — pasta, rice, or dehydrated meal with hot drink

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is long and can be wet — Fiordland averages over 6,000mm of rain per year. Waterproof gear is essential. The track is well-marked but can be slippery. Take your time and enjoy the waterfalls — there are hundreds after rainfall.

day_by_day.morning: The highlight day: 14 km from Mintaro Hut over the famous Mackinnon Pass (1,154m) to Dumpling Hut. The climb to the pass is steep but rewarded with 360-degree views of Fiordland on a clear day. Visit the Mackinnon Pass memorial and shelter at the top.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the dramatic zigzag trail down to the Arthur Valley. Pass the spectacular Sutherland Falls — at 580m, one of the tallest waterfalls in the world — and take the optional 30-minute side trip to the base. Arrive at Dumpling Hut.
day_by_day.evening: This is the most celebrated evening on the track — celebrate crossing the pass with fellow hikers. Cook a special dinner and enjoy the sense of achievement.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked early breakfast — start hiking early to make the most of clear morning weather on the pass
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Mackinnon Pass shelter — pack extra snacks for the big day
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hut dinner — treat yourself to your best trail meal to celebrate the pass

day_by_day.notes: Mackinnon Pass can be closed due to extreme weather or snow even in November. DOC rangers will advise if conditions are dangerous. Always follow ranger instructions. The descent to Dumpling Hut is steep and hard on knees — trekking poles are highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Final day: 18 km from Dumpling Hut to Sandfly Point. Walk through lush rainforest with giant ferns, moss-covered trees, and the roaring sounds of the Arthur River. Pass the Boatshed and the Giant Gate Falls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Sandfly Point — the end of the Milford Track. Ring the famous bell and celebrate completing one of the world's greatest walks! Take the ferry across to Milford Sound. Explore Milford Sound briefly and arrange transport back to Te Anau (approximately 2 hours by bus).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau, check in to accommodation, shower, and celebrate with a proper restaurant meal. Your legs will be tired but your spirit will be soaring.

meals.breakfast: Early self-cooked breakfast at Dumpling Hut — use up remaining trail food
meals.lunch: Final trail lunch at Sandfly Point or on the ferry
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a Te Anau restaurant — you deserve it! Try the Fiordland Bakery or Ristorante Pizzeria Paradiso (~NZD $30–$50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The ferry from Sandfly Point to Milford Sound is included in your track pass. Book your bus transfer from Milford Sound back to Te Anau in advance. The road between Milford Sound and Te Anau (SH94) is stunning — try to sit on the right side of the bus for the best views through the Homer Tunnel.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day after the Milford Track. Sleep in and have a late, leisurely breakfast. Take a gentle flat walk along the Te Anau lakefront to gently stretch your legs. Visit the Te Anau DOC Visitor Centre to learn more about Fiordland's unique ecology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic cruise on Milford Sound (day trip from Te Anau — approximately 2.5 hours drive each way, or join a coach tour). A Milford Sound cruise showcases towering fiord walls, cascading waterfalls, and wildlife including dolphins, seals, and penguins. Alternatively, stay in Te Anau and take a scenic flight over Fiordland if budget allows.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau for a final evening in Fiordland. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and pack your bags for the drive back north tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at a Te Anau café — reward yourself after the track (~NZD $20–$30)
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the Milford Sound cruise or a packed lunch if driving independently (~NZD $15–$25)
meals.dinner: Te Anau's Sandfly Café or The Moose — casual mid-range dining with a warm atmosphere (~NZD $35–$50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: A Milford Sound cruise is an absolute highlight — even if you've just walked the Milford Track, seeing the fiord from the water is a completely different and equally stunning experience. Book the cruise in advance. The road to Milford Sound is one of the most scenic drives in New Zealand.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Te Anau accommodation and begin the drive back toward your resort/Queenstown. Stop at the Mirror Lakes on SH94 for a short walk and stunning reflections of the Earl Mountains. Continue to Queenstown for a final morning coffee and browse of the town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Spend a final relaxing afternoon on the beachfront — swim, sunbathe, or simply sit and reflect on an incredible 13-day adventure. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at local boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner at the resort or a nearby restaurant. Celebrate an extraordinary trip — from the highest bungy in New Zealand to the world's greatest walk. Pack for departure and arrange any transfers needed for your onward journey.

meals.breakfast: Final Te Anau café breakfast before checkout (~NZD $18–$25)
meals.lunch: Roadside café or Queenstown stop for a farewell lunch — try a classic New Zealand meat pie or café meal (~NZD $15–$25)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby mid-range restaurant — splurge slightly on your last night with New Zealand lamb and a local Pinot Noir (~NZD $50–$70 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for the drive back as the scenery is beautiful and you'll want to stop for photos. Confirm any departure transfers or rental car return arrangements. New Zealand's South Island will leave a lasting impression — start planning your return trip!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience includes a scenic gondola ride to the pod suspended above the canyon and is a must-do for adrenaline seekers visiting Queenstown.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most spectacular and famous one-day walks, crossing volcanic terrain with emerald crater lakes, steaming vents, and panoramic views of the Central Plateau. The 19.4 km trail passes the active Mount Ngauruhoe and offers otherworldly landscapes that inspired the Lord of the Rings films.

experiences.name: Milford Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Embark on a multi-day guided or independent hike along the world-famous Milford Track, a 53.5 km trail through Fiordland National Park. Trek through ancient rainforests, past cascading waterfalls including the stunning Sutherland Falls, and over the dramatic MacKinnon Pass with breathtaking alpine views.

experiences.name: Roys Peak Track Hike
experiences.description: Conquer the iconic Roys Peak trail above Lake Wānaka for one of the most photographed panoramic views in New Zealand. The 16 km round-trip hike rewards trekkers with sweeping vistas of Lake Wānaka, Mount Aspiring National Park, and the surrounding Southern Alps, especially magical at sunrise.

experiences.name: Shotover Canyon Swing
experiences.description: Experience the world's highest cliff jump and canyon swing, launching 109 meters above the wild Shotover River in Queenstown. With over 70 jump styles to choose from, this thrilling activity combines freefall with a massive pendulum swing through a dramatic schist rock canyon, offering an unforgettable adrenaline rush.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch or Queenstown Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome amenity (champagne and light bites prepared by the resort). Late-night room service available.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or airport lounge dining
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated cheese board, antipasto platter, and New Zealand Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in preparation so the room is fully ready upon late arrival. Keep Day 2 morning relaxed to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast overlooking the beachfront. Take a gentle orientation walk along the shoreline to acclimatize and soak in the South Island scenery. Visit the resort spa for a 60-minute jet-lag recovery massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided scenic drive through the surrounding region — explore local viewpoints, vineyards, and landscapes with a knowledgeable local guide. Stop at a boutique winery for a premium tasting of Central Otago Pinot Noir.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's beachfront terrace. Fine dining at the resort's signature restaurant featuring locally sourced New Zealand cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — eggs benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit, artisan pastries, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Light grazing lunch at the winery — artisan bread, local cheeses, charcuterie, and paired wines
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — pan-seared South Island salmon, Canterbury lamb rack, and a curated New Zealand wine list

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery day. Avoid strenuous activities. Confirm bookings for upcoming experiences — Nevis Bungy, Milford Track, and Roys Peak — with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Roys Peak Track Hike above Lake Wānaka. Depart by 6:00 AM to beat the crowds and catch the golden morning light. The 16 km return trail ascends 1,279 meters and rewards hikers with one of New Zealand's most iconic panoramic views over Lake Wānaka and the Southern Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Roys Peak and return to Wānaka township. Explore the charming lakeside town — browse galleries, boutique shops, and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere. Visit Puzzling World or simply relax by the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Freshen up and enjoy a restorative dinner at a premium Wānaka restaurant before heading back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed luxury trail breakfast prepared by the resort — thermos of coffee, smoked salmon bagels, energy bars, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at Francesca's Italian Kitchen, Wānaka — wood-fired pizza, fresh pasta, and Italian wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ritual Café & Bar or Bistro Gentil, Wānaka — slow-roasted duck, local venison, and Central Otago wines

day_by_day.notes: Start the hike very early (6:00 AM) to avoid crowds and enjoy the best photography light at the iconic viewpoint. Wear layers as summit temperatures can be cool even in November. Hiking poles recommended. Ensure premium hiking gear is packed the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest morning — enjoy the resort's beachfront facilities, swim, or take a stand-up paddleboard session on the water. Optional: resort yoga class or stretching session to recover legs from Roys Peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Helicopter scenic flight over the Southern Alps and Fiordland — a premium 60–90 minute private charter offering aerial views of glaciers, fiords, and mountain peaks that few travelers ever witness up close.
day_by_day.evening: Private chef's table dinner experience at Aegean Bliss Resort — a bespoke multi-course tasting menu prepared exclusively for your group, paired with premium New Zealand and international wines.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — fresh-baked pastries, cold cuts, eggs to order, smoothies, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: In-flight catering on the helicopter (premium picnic box) or light lunch at the resort pool bar upon return
meals.dinner: Chef's table at Aegean Bliss Resort — 7-course tasting menu featuring Bluff oysters, South Island crayfish, Canterbury lamb, and Akaroa salmon

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter scenic flight well in advance as availability is limited. Weather-dependent — the resort concierge should have a backup plan (e.g., 4WD alpine safari). Chef's table requires advance reservation with dietary requirements submitted.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer to Queenstown (approximately 1 hour by private luxury vehicle). Check in luggage at a premium Queenstown hotel or use the resort's concierge luggage service. Morning at leisure in Queenstown — stroll along the lakefront promenade and explore the vibrant town center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nevis Bungy Jump — Experience New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. A thrilling 8.5-second freefall in one of the most dramatic landscapes in the Southern Hemisphere. Private transport to the Nevis platform is included.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the jump with cocktails at a Queenstown rooftop bar. Premium dinner at one of Queenstown's finest restaurants overlooking Lake Wakatipu.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure — full cooked breakfast with eggs, bacon, avocado, and sourdough toast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Queenstown's Rata Restaurant (chef Josh Emett) — modern New Zealand cuisine with local ingredients
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amisfield Winery & Bistro or Botswana Butchery, Queenstown — premium dry-aged steaks, fresh seafood, and exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy requires pre-booking through AJ Hackett. Weight and health restrictions apply — confirm eligibility in advance. Wear comfortable, secure clothing for the jump. GoPro footage package recommended for memories. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort by private transfer in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Shotover Canyon Swing — Launch 109 meters above the wild Shotover River in the world's highest cliff jump and canyon swing. Multiple jump styles available for varying levels of daring. Located near Queenstown, accessible by private transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Recovery and adrenaline celebration — Queenstown gondola ride to the Skyline complex for panoramic views over the Remarkables and Lake Wakatipu. Optional luge rides or simply enjoy the views with a glass of bubbles.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset lake cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard a luxury charter vessel — champagne, canapés, and breathtaking mountain reflections on the water.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a Queenstown café — avocado toast, acai bowls, and cold brew coffee at Vudu Café or Bespoke Kitchen
meals.lunch: Skyline Restaurant buffet at the gondola summit — panoramic views with a wide selection of New Zealand-inspired dishes
meals.dinner: Canapés and champagne on the lake cruise, followed by dinner at The Bunker Restaurant, Queenstown — intimate fine dining with an exceptional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book Shotover Canyon Swing and lake cruise well in advance. Combine both Nevis Bungy and Canyon Swing into a two-day adrenaline sequence for maximum excitement. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort via private transfer after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend time at the spa. Full-body deep tissue massage or hot stone therapy to prepare the body for the upcoming Milford Track multi-day hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gear check and preparation for the Milford Track Great Walk beginning the next day. Resort concierge assists with packing luxury hiking essentials — premium rain gear, merino wool layers, and trekking poles. Afternoon briefing with the private guided hiking company.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner and early bedtime in preparation for the Milford Track departure. Quiet evening at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast — eggs florentine, smoked salmon, fresh fruit platter, and French press coffee
meals.lunch: Resort pool bar lunch — gourmet sandwiches, salads, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Early dinner at the resort restaurant — light but nourishing pre-trek meal of grilled fish, roasted vegetables, and brown rice, with herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Milford Track Great Walk requires Great Walks passes booked months in advance through DOC (Department of Conservation). Guided walk option (through Ultimate Hikes) provides luxury lodge accommodation along the track — strongly recommended for a premium experience. Pack bags tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer to Te Anau for the start of the Milford Track Great Walk. Private luxury coach or charter flight to Te Anau. Board the boat across Lake Te Anau to Glade Wharf — the official start of the track. Begin hiking through ancient beech forest along the Clinton River (5 km, easy terrain).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through lush rainforest, spotting native birds including kea, fantails, and tūī. Arrive at Clinton Hut (guided lodge) by mid-afternoon. Settle in, freshen up, and explore the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Guided lodge dinner prepared by on-site chefs — hearty New Zealand cuisine with wine. Evening talk by the guide about the track's ecology and history.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Te Anau lodge before departure — full cooked breakfast with eggs, toast, cereals, and hot drinks
meals.lunch: Trail lunch pack provided by the guided operator — gourmet sandwiches, trail mix, fruit, and chocolate
meals.dinner: Clinton Hut lodge dinner — roast lamb, seasonal vegetables, fresh bread, and New Zealand wine

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 of the Milford Track is relatively gentle (5 km). Weather can change rapidly — waterproof gear is essential. The guided (Ultimate Hikes) experience provides private lodges, hot showers, and meals, making it a true luxury wilderness experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Clinton Hut and hike through the Clinton Valley toward the base of Mackinnon Pass (16.5 km, moderate terrain). Pass through stunning beech forest and open valley floors with dramatic mountain walls on either side.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Mintaro Hut (guided lodge) by early afternoon. Relax, enjoy the scenery, and prepare mentally for the challenging Mackinnon Pass crossing the following morning.
day_by_day.evening: Lodge dinner with fellow hikers. Guide presentation on Mackinnon Pass history and what to expect on Day 3.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast at Clinton Hut — porridge, eggs, toast, fresh fruit, and hot drinks
meals.lunch: Trail lunch pack — wraps, energy bars, dried fruit, nuts, and thermos of soup
meals.dinner: Mintaro Hut lodge dinner — beef stew, roasted potatoes, salad, dessert, and wine

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is a longer day (16.5 km). Pace yourself and enjoy the incredible valley scenery. November weather in Fiordland can bring rain — embrace it as part of the authentic experience. Waterfall sightings are more dramatic after rain.

day_by_day.morning: The most dramatic day — ascend Mackinnon Pass (1,154 m), the highest point of the Milford Track. Breathtaking panoramic views of the Fiordland wilderness (weather permitting). Descend through alpine meadows and past the spectacular Sutherland Falls — one of the tallest waterfalls in the world at 580 meters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descent to Dumpling Hut (guided lodge) — total distance approximately 14 km. Arrive by mid-afternoon, soak tired legs, and celebrate completing the most iconic section of the track.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory lodge dinner — the guides often mark the Mackinnon Pass crossing with a special meal and drinks.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast at Mintaro Hut — full cooked breakfast to fuel the big climb
meals.lunch: Summit picnic lunch at Mackinnon Pass shelter — hot soup from thermos, gourmet sandwiches, chocolate, and energy snacks
meals.dinner: Dumpling Hut lodge dinner — celebratory meal with premium wine, roast chicken, seasonal vegetables, and pavlova dessert

day_by_day.notes: Mackinnon Pass can be snowy or icy even in November — microspikes may be needed. The guided operator will advise on conditions. The detour to Sutherland Falls adds approximately 1 hour but is absolutely worth it. This is the highlight of the entire Milford Track.

day_by_day.morning: Final day of the Milford Track — hike the last 18 km through rainforest, past giant ferns, and along the Arthur River to Sandfly Point at Milford Sound. This section passes through lush lowland forest and crosses several swing bridges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Sandfly Point and board the boat across to Milford Sound. Celebrate completing the world-famous Milford Track with a scenic cruise on Milford Sound — towering fiord walls, Mitre Peak, cascading waterfalls, and resident dolphins and seals.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer back to Te Anau and then to Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrive at the resort for a well-deserved hot bath, room service, and rest.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast at Dumpling Hut — eggs, bacon, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Celebration lunch on the Milford Sound cruise boat — seafood platter, sandwiches, and sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — comfort meal of pasta, garlic bread, and a bottle of Central Otago Pinot Noir delivered to the room

day_by_day.notes: The final day is the longest in distance (18 km) but relatively flat. Sandflies at Sandfly Point are notorious — bring strong insect repellent. The Milford Sound cruise is included in most guided Milford Track packages. Private transfer back to the resort should be pre-arranged.

day_by_day.morning: Full recovery day at Aegean Bliss Resort. Sleep in, enjoy a luxurious spa morning — book a 90-minute couples or solo spa package including a deep tissue massage, facial, and hydrotherapy soak to restore tired muscles after four days of hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon by the resort pool or on the beachfront. Optional: private wine tasting experience hosted at the resort, featuring a curated selection of South Island's finest Pinot Noirs, Sauvignon Blancs, and Rieslings with a sommelier guide.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the resort bar. Premium final dinner at the resort's finest dining outlet — a celebratory meal reflecting on an extraordinary South Island adventure.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent late breakfast at the resort — eggs benedict, smoked salmon, fresh berries, pastries, and champagne
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — sushi platter, prawn cocktail, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Celebratory fine dining dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — 5-course degustation menu with wine pairing: Bluff oysters, South Island crayfish bisque, Akaroa salmon, Canterbury lamb, and a New Zealand cheese board to finish

day_by_day.notes: This is a full rest and recovery day — essential after the Milford Track. Use the day to reflect, journal, and prepare for departure the following day. Pack bags in the evening. Arrange checkout and airport transfer with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a last leisurely breakfast with beachfront views. Take a slow walk along the shore for a final farewell to the South Island's stunning scenery. Checkout from the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to the airport. Depending on departure time, enjoy the airport's premium lounge with complimentary food, drinks, and Wi-Fi. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day South Island adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry memories of Roys Peak sunrises, Nevis freefall, Shotover Canyon thrills, and four days walking the world-famous Milford Track through one of Earth's last great wilderness areas.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full à la carte spread with fresh juice, eggs to order, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge dining or in-flight business class meal
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure transfer timing with concierge the night before. Allow extra time at the airport for international departures. Consider purchasing local souvenirs — Manuka honey, Central Otago wines, and merino wool products make excellent gifts. Request a late checkout if the flight departs in the afternoon.
